claim: No federal pre-market drug approval system existed before 1938
method: Read the 1906 Food and Drugs Act in full (U.S. Statutes at Large via govinfo.gov)
observed_value: The 1906 Act prohibits manufacturing/interstate shipment of adulterated or misbranded drugs and enforces by notice, certification to the district attorney, seizure and criminal penalty. It creates no application, no filing and no approval. Examinations are assigned to the Bureau of Chemistry, Department of Agriculture (Sec. 4).
verification_status: Verified - statute text retrieved and read from govinfo.gov
notes: Consequence for this project: there is no such thing as an 'FDA approval decision' before the 1938 FD&C Act, so a pre-1938 decision table would necessarily be invented. None is written.

claim: Federal pre-market LICENSURE of one drug class predates the FDA by 36 years
method: Read the Biologics Control Act of 1902 in full (U.S. Statutes at Large via govinfo.gov)
observed_value: From six months after the regulations were promulgated, no virus, therapeutic serum, toxin, antitoxin or analogous product for the prevention and cure of human disease may be sold in or shipped into the District of Columbia or across state lines unless made at an establishment holding an unsuspended, unrevoked license issued by the Secretary of the Treasury, and unless each package bears the proper name, manufacturer name, address, license number and an expiration date.
verification_status: Verified - statute text retrieved and read from govinfo.gov
notes: This is the only pre-1938 federal drug pre-market authorisation regime. It was administered by the Public Health Service, not by FDA; biologics authority moved to FDA in 1972. No official machine-readable census of individual 1902-1938 licenses is published, so no per-license rows are asserted anywhere in this repository - documented as an open data gap, not filled by inference.

claim: The new-drug application was created by the 1938 FD&C Act
method: Read the enacting chapter in the U.S. Statutes at Large (govinfo.gov) and the current codification at 21 U.S.C. 355(a)
observed_value: Act of June 25, 1938, ch. 675, 52 Stat. 1040; Sec. 1: 'This Act may be cited as the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.' Now 21 U.S.C. 355(a): 'No person shall introduce or deliver for introduction into interstate commerce any new drug, unless an approval of an application filed pursuant to subsection (b) or (j) is effective with respect to such drug.'
verification_status: Verified - statute text and codification retrieved and read
notes: This is why the project's verified decision coverage begins in 1939: the application system itself began in 1938, and the official database's first recorded action is 1939-02-09. 21 U.S.C. 355 codification read at https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title21-section355&num=0&edition=prelim
